newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower in line with soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower in line with soybeans.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended lower, in line with losses in soybeans, with heavy fund selling noted, traders said.
"We broke stops late in meal and oil. The weather is still bearish and funds were big sellers especially in beans and meal," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Soybeans broke late as bearish crop production forecasts included in President Bill Clinton's proposed fiscal 1998 budget hit a skittish market.
The budget included projections for 64 million soybean acres next year with production at 2.42 billion bushels.
Later in the afternoon, USDA analysts said actual acreage will likely be even higher, noting the figures were based on outdated data taken from the November crop report.
Soymeal ended down $3.40 to $0.50 per ton with March off $3.40 at $232.50. Soyoil closed down 0.13 to 0.04 cent per lb with March down 0.13 at 23.86 cents.
Funds sold at least 1,100 lots soymeal on the day which put that market on the defensive. Rosenthal Collins sold 1,000 lots March soymeal while Dean Witter sold 400 lots.
Weather in South America was also cited as a bearish factor.
Forecasts called for more rains in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul region and in central Argentina. Drier conditions were expected in Parana where harvest should be underway soon.
Weekly export sales data further pressured the market.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soymeal during the week ended January 30 totaled 52,000 tonnes, near the low end of expectations for 50,000 to 70,000 tonnes.
Net sales of soyoil totaled 5,700 tonnes, below expectations for 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes.
The sales report showed China cancelled 53,000 tonnes U.S. soymeal purchases. That news, coupled with reports of poor Chinese demand, pushed soymeal prices lower.

With many Chinese ports clogged with imported soybean meal and the country closing down for the Lunar New Year festival, Far East grain traders told Reuters their only recent activity has been watching domestic soymeal prices fall.
Up to 500,000 tonnes of soymeal remain in China's ports, most of it in the south where it is deteriorating due to damp winter weather, Asian traders said.

On the day, ADM sold 400 lots May soymeal and one lots March. Cargill Inc bought 300 lots March but sold 200 March and 100 May. Central Soya, Term Commodities and Produce Grain were all small-lot buyers, traders said.
In soyoil, ADM bought 400 lots March and sold 450 lots May. Produce Grain bought 300 March and Term Commodities bought 200 March.
In options trade, Prudential Securities reportedly sold 1,200 May 24.00 cent puts, traders said.

Soymeal volume was estimated at 19,000 lots, against Wednesday's actual volume of 16,240 lots, CBOT reported. Soyoil volume pegged at 14,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 16,569 lots.
